findings.title: BlockedEmail match_count/last_match_at are double-counted per signup attempt
findings.body: In UsersController#create, `user.valid?` is called explicitly (line 168) and then `user.save` is called again a few lines later (line 172). Rails reruns all validations on every call to valid?/save, so the new EmailValidator (and therefore BlockedEmail.should_block?, which mutates and saves the matched BlockedEmail row) executes twice per request. This means `match_count` is incremented by 2 instead of 1 and `last_match_at`/the extra `BlockedEmail` lookup+save happen twice for every single signup attempt (not just discourse-hub flows, since `user.valid?` is evaluated unconditionally due to `&&` short-circuit order). This corrupts the statistics the feature is meant to produce and doubles the DB load added by this feature on every signup.

findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, allowing trivial bypass
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` performs an exact, case-sensitive string match against the stored email. Since email addresses are effectively case-insensitive, a spammer whose address was blocked (e.g. `spam@example.com`) can bypass the block entirely simply by submitting `Spam@Example.com` or any other casing variant. This defeats the purpose of the feature. The whitelist/blacklist domain check in lib/validators/email_validator.rb uses a case-insensitive regex, but the new block-list lookup does not normalize case at all.

findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write race on match_count
findings.body: should_block? loads the BlockedEmail row, increments `match_count` in Ruby, then calls `save`. Two concurrent signup requests for the same blocked email can both read the same `match_count` value before either writes back, so one increment is silently lost (classic lost-update race). The statistic is also not updated atomically with respect to `last_match_at`. This should use an atomic DB update (e.g. `update_counters`, `increment!`, or a raw SQL `UPDATE ... SET match_count = match_count + 1`) instead of a load-then-save round trip.

findings.title: rejectedEmails array is a shared mutable default shared across controller instances
findings.body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is declared as a plain property value in `.extend()`, so this exact array object is evaluated once at class-definition time and shared by the prototype. `createAccount` later calls `pushObject` on it (line 275), mutating the shared array in place. Any new instance of CreateAccountController created later (e.g. if the modal controller is re-instantiated) will see emails rejected by a completely unrelated prior session/instance, incorrectly failing emailValidation for emails that were never rejected for that instance. The array should be initialized per-instance in an `init()` hook instead of as a literal default value.

findings.title: No end-to-end test for blocked-email signup rejection or new response fields
findings.body: The create action now returns `errors` and `values` fields on failure specifically to support the new client-side rejectedEmails tracking, and signups are expected to be rejected when the submitted email matches a BlockedEmail record. There is no request/controller spec asserting that POST /users with a blocked email is rejected and that the JSON response includes the `errors`/`values` keys the JS controller depends on. Only the isolated EmailValidator and BlockedEmail model specs exist, so the full integration path (controller -> User#valid? -> EmailValidator -> BlockedEmail) is untested.

findings.title: EmailValidator spec omits whitelist/blacklist coverage removed from User model
findings.body: The domain whitelist/blacklist validation logic previously lived in User#email_validator/email_in_restriction_setting? and is now moved into EmailValidator (lib/validators/email_validator.rb), but this new spec file only exercises the 'blocked email' branch. There is no test verifying `email_domains_whitelist`/`email_domains_blacklist` behavior still works correctly after being relocated out of user.rb, leaving that previously-tested logic without direct validator-level coverage.

findings.title: New rejectedEmails client logic has no test coverage
findings.body: The new rejectedEmails tracking in emailValidation (lines 69-74) and the pushObject call in createAccount (lines 274-276) introduce new client-visible behavior that gates form submission, but no JS unit test was added to verify that a rejected email correctly fails emailValidation/submitDisabled or that successful resubmission with a different email clears the failure.
